questions.q: What does installing the Kubeflow Training Operator actually give you?
options: A pre-trained language model ready to fine-tune
A controller that watches for PyTorchJob objects and turns them into the right number of Pods, configured correctly
A GPU driver installer
A replacement for Kubernetes itself
questions.explain: The Training Operator is the controller responsible for reconciling a PyTorchJob's spec into the actual master and worker Pods, with the right environment variables set.

questions.q: In the capstone's PyTorchJob manifest, how do you run the exercise entirely on CPU instead of GPU?
options: Set replicas to 0
Remove the nvidia.com/gpu entry from resources, and use the gloo backend in the training script
CPU-only training is not possible with PyTorchJob
Change the apiVersion to v1beta1
questions.explain: Dropping the GPU resource request and switching the process group backend to gloo (PyTorch's CPU-compatible distributed backend) lets the same manifest and script pattern run without GPUs.

questions.q: Why shouldn't you manually set MASTER_ADDR, RANK, and WORLD_SIZE in the capstone's training script?
options: Those variables don't exist in PyTorch
The Kubeflow Training Operator injects them automatically into every Pod based on the replica spec
They are deprecated and no longer used by torch.distributed
Setting them manually always causes a crash
questions.explain: The Training Operator sets these environment variables per Pod automatically; the training script just reads them via torch.distributed, the same as on solara-train.

questions.q: How can you confirm the capstone job is genuinely running as a distributed job rather than four independent copies of the same script?
options: Check that the Docker image size is under 1 GB
Confirm that dist.get_world_size() reports 4 and each Pod reports a distinct dist.get_rank()
Check that the job's name contains the word 'distributed'
There is no way to verify this
questions.explain: A genuinely distributed job reports a consistent world_size across all processes, each with its own unique rank — confirming they've joined one process group, not run in isolation.

questions.q: What role does MinIO play in this capstone if you're running entirely on a local `kind` cluster?
options: It replaces the Kubeflow Training Operator
It provides an S3-API-compatible object storage endpoint so torch.distributed.checkpoint has somewhere to save to, without needing a real cloud account
It is a GPU emulator for machines without a GPU
It monitors GPU utilization in place of DCGM
questions.explain: MinIO implements the S3 API locally, letting the same dcp.save()/dcp.load() checkpoint code work against a local stand-in instead of a real S3 bucket.
